question: Which tissue is responsible for the movement in our body?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Muscular tissue**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Muscular tissue** is responsible for the **movement in our body**.
 
• There are three types of muscular tissue: **skeletal, smooth, and cardiac muscles**.
 
• **Skeletal muscles** are attached to bones and are responsible for voluntary movements.
 
• **Smooth muscles** are found in the walls of internal organs and help in involuntary movements such as digestion.
 
• **Cardiac muscles** are found in the heart and are responsible for pumping blood throughout the body.
 
• Muscular tissues can contract and relax, which allows them to produce movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Epithelial tissue**__

 __
 
• **Epithelial tissue** covers the outer surfaces of organs and blood vessels throughout the body, as well as the inner surfaces of cavities in many internal organs.
 
• It acts as a barrier to protect the body from outside invaders and helps in absorption, secretion, and sensation.
 
 
 
• **Cartilage**__
 __
 
• **Cartilage** is a flexible connective tissue found in various parts of the body including joints, ear, nose, and bronchial tubes.
 
• It provides support and cushioning in the joints and reduces friction between bones.
 
 
 
• **Areolar tissue**__
 
 
• **Areolar tissue** is a type of connective tissue that holds organs in place and attaches epithelial tissue to underlying tissues.
 
• It also serves as a reservoir of water and salts for surrounding tissues.
